$comment: Bangladesh region pack — Wave 1 launch market.
PRD §1.2: 'If a new country requires a code change, the architecture has
failed.' Everything region-specific lives in a file like this one: food DB,
portion units, GI table, risk calibration, cutoffs, units, language, meal
slots, safety thresholds. Adding a market ships a pack plus a validation
set — never a retrain, never a branch in application code.
$language_note: Bangla is the default when device locale is bn (PRD F13). Both must be complete — no clipped Bangla, no untranslated strings (PRD §18).

units_default.$note: numerals may be 'bengali' (১২৩) per user preference (PRD F13). Canonical SI is always what gets stored; this is display only.

anthropometric_cutoffs.$comment: Asian-Pacific, NOT Western. Playbook §B9 calls this the single highest-leverage change for real-world accuracy in this population — larger than any hyperparameter sweep.

waist_to_height_ratio.$note: Travels across ethnicities better than BMI. Same threshold everywhere, which is precisely why it is valuable.

anthropometric_cutoffs.$age_note: Risk onset is roughly a decade earlier than in Western cohorts. Do not transplant a US age curve.

risk_model.$clinical_score_note: IDRS is the Layer-1 anchor for South Asia — four items, validated in Indian populations, and its waist thresholds are already South-Asian-appropriate.
risk_model.$validation_note: PRD §7.4b: while this reads 'not_validated', the UI MUST degrade to the transparent clinical score and say so. Never quietly guess. Flips to 'provisional' once DiaBD hold-out metrics exist, and to 'validated' after local clinical validation.

prevalence_prior.source: IDF Diabetes Atlas — country-level adult (20–79) prevalence
prevalence_prior.$todo: Fill from the current IDF Atlas edition and record the edition + page. Left null deliberately: a wrong prevalence prior silently miscalibrates every probability shown to every user in this market, and a guessed value is worse than an absent one.

risk_model.$blend_note: final = w·calibrated_GBM + (1−w)·clinical_score, w tuned on validation (Playbook §B8, typically 0.6–0.75). Placeholder until Stage 2 tunes it.

food.composition_source: Food Composition Table for Bangladesh (2013), INFS, University of Dhaka
food.$blocker: Commercial redistribution needs written INFS permission (docs/licensing.md). This blocks the food pack, which blocks food logging entirely.
food.$portion_note: Gram equivalents come from standardised Bangladeshi serving guidelines and are per-food, not global — a বাটি of ভাত is not a বাটি of ডাল. Nulls here are honest placeholders.

ramadan.$safety: Fasting with diabetes carries real risk. Entering Ramadan mode must surface a safety card advising the user to consult their doctor before fasting (PRD F13), and must not present a calorie deficit target during the fast.

safety_thresholds.$comment: PRD §3.3 red-flag interceptor. These are absolute clinical values, not preferences. A region pack may make them STRICTER, never looser.
safety_thresholds.$emergency_note: Bangladesh national emergency service. Every market must set this before launch (PRD §18).

features.$clinician_note: Off until F16 ships and the intended-purpose document is reviewed. Bangladesh has no mature SaMD regime for wellness apps, so this is the lowest-friction market to enable it in first — but not before the feature exists.
features.$feature_note: All false for the Stage 4 vertical slice. Flags exist now so enabling them later is config, not a release branch.

regulatory.regime: no mature SaMD regime for wellness apps
regulatory.$wording_note: PRD §3.5: Bangladesh may say 'diabetes risk'. Regulated markets get a different string pack ('metabolic health score') for the same model. Same code, different intended purpose, different words.
